unmapped_findings: Fe0.75Mn0.25Al is classified as ductile by the B/G criterion: its B/G ratio of 1.91 exceeds the 1.75 threshold, whereas FeAl (1.56) and Fe0.875Mn0.125Al (1.75) are brittle (b0045).

In the reported descending anisotropy order, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al ranks between Fe0.375Mn0.625Al and Fe0.25Mn0.75Al: MnAl > Fe0.5Mn0.5Al > Fe0.625Mn0.375Al > Fe0.125Mn0.875Al > Fe0.375Mn0.625Al > Fe0.75Mn0.25Al > Fe0.25Mn0.75Al > Fe0.875Mn0.125Al > FeAl (b0059).
Fe0.75Mn0.25Al satisfies the cubic mechanical stability criteria (C11-C12 > 0, C11 > 0, C44 > 0, C11+2C12 > 0), confirming it is mechanically stable (b0033, b0034).

For Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, the band from -5 to 1 eV is dominated by Al-p, Fe-d and Mn-d states; near the Fermi level the Fermi surface arises mainly from Fe-d and Mn-d states with low Al-p hybridization (b0028).

The Fig. 4 electron-density panels are captioned only as 'Fe Mn Al-(011)' and 'Fe Mn Al-(110)' without explicit composition subscripts; the panel pair (c)/(d) is assumed to correspond to Fe0.75Mn0.25Al by lettering convention, but this is not explicitly stated in the caption (b0043, figure_004).
